title: Auditing Norm-Clipped L2-Laplacian Token-Embedding Obfuscation Against Sequence-Aware Reconstruction

contributions.purpose: Show that the norm-clipped L2-Laplacian embedding defense provides no meaningful privacy at its proposed operating point.
contributions.mechanism: Audits the defense (eta=142, 30-50% clip rate) against both a per-token nearest-neighbor (NN) attack and the sequence-aware BeamClean attacker, demonstrating a ceiling effect.
contributions.evaluation: Both attackers achieve near-perfect reconstruction: >99.98% Token-ASR and 100% Canary-EM.
contributions.domain: Privacy defenses for text embeddings in split/remote NLP inference.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate a ceiling effect: at the proposed operating point, both simple and sophisticated attackers achieve near-perfect reconstruction, rendering the defense ineffective.

contributions.purpose: Compare sophisticated vs simple attackers under this defense.
contributions.mechanism: Directly benchmarks BeamClean (LM-prior sequence-aware) against nearest-neighbor decoding under norm-clipped perturbation.
contributions.evaluation: BeamClean does not outperform NN; NN achieves marginally higher accuracy due to the ceiling effect (comparison becomes moot).
contributions.domain: Privacy defenses for text embeddings in split/remote NLP inference.
contributions.source_quote: We show that BeamClean does not outperform NN under norm-clipped perturbation; in fact, NN achieves marginally higher accuracy due to the ceiling effect.

contributions.mechanism: Directional preservation analysis showing norm clipping preserves embedding direction exactly, and NN lookup depends only on direction.
contributions.evaluation: Explains that simple NN attacks suffice when noise is mild; implies defenses must perturb directional information, not just magnitude.
contributions.domain: Privacy defenses for text embeddings in split/remote NLP inference.
contributions.source_quote: We explain this finding through directional preservation analysis: norm clipping preserves directional information exactly, making simple NN attacks sufficient when noise is mild.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work extends this line of research by auditing reconstruction attacks specifically against norm-clipped perturbation mechanisms.

Recent work on BeamClean (Kale et al., 2025) has shown that sequence-aware attacks leveraging language model priors can dramatically outperform NN baselines under input-independent noise -- but BeamClean's evaluation did not include norm-clipped mechanisms.

Our work contributes to this empirical evaluation paradigm by auditing reconstruction attacks under specific defense mechanisms, revealing that theoretical privacy guarantees may not translate to practical protection when the noise level is insufficient.

notes: Negative/audit result: the audited defense provides no meaningful privacy protection (ceiling effect). Tie-like result: the sophisticated BeamClean attacker does NOT beat the simple NN baseline (NN marginally higher) because both saturate near 100%.
